lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: This is Every Possible News. Deadpan news, from every possible tonight.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Every Possible News. If it happened anywhere, it happened here. Probably to you.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: You're listening to Every Possible News! Weather, traffic and the news, in that order, or any other order!

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: This is Kim Harrowgate, standing in it, for Every Possible News.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Every Possible News is brought to you by Grumbel's Ladders.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Up is a choice.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Every Possible News. Unflappable, since the very first flap.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: You're listening to Every Possible News. All of it is true somewhere. Some of it is true here.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Every Possible News. It is eleven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It is always eleven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good evening, or whatever it is where you are. This is Every Possible News. I'm Dale Quarterly, and this is the news, from wherever you are.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Our top story. Scientists in Dimension Four B have confirmed that the thing in your attic is, in fact, you, from next Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Officials say there is no cause for alarm, and ask that you stop going up there, because you are making yourself uncomfortable.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: In economic news, the price of gravity rose sharply this afternoon, before falling, as is its nature.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Residents across the eastern Overlap report that the moon has been looking at them. A spokesperson for the moon declined to comment, but continued looking.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: And finally. A man has been named employee of the month for the four hundredth consecutive month. He does not work here. We are looking into it.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That's the news. More at eleven. It is always eleven.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Our top story tonight: the collapse. For more, we go live to Kim Harrowgate, who is standing in it. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Thanks, Dale. I'm here at the scene, which is also, technically, every scene.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Authorities tell me the collapse began at approximately four in the afternoon, and has since begun at several other times as well. Residents are being told to remain calm, or, failing that, to remain.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim, is anyone hurt?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, nobody here has the concept of hurt. It's actually very nice. A man just handed me a soup. I don't know why. I'm going to eat it.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim, please don't eat the soup.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Back to you—

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We appear to have lost Kim. Our thoughts are with the soup.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A shadow has been seen in Founders Park without a person attached. Kim Harrowgate is there now. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm standing next to the bench where the shadow was last seen. It sat here most of the afternoon, feeding pigeons that weren't there.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Witnesses say it seemed calm, and a little taller than when it left home.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Do we know whose shadow it is?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: We do, Dale. It answers to Greg. It belongs to a Mister Hollis Fenn of the eastern Overlap, who has been without a shadow since a Tuesday in the spring.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Mister Fenn has asked me to say, on air, that he isn't angry. And that the porch light is on.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Has anyone tried to approach it?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: A park keeper tried, Dale. Greg simply stepped into the shade of an oak tree and was, for all practical purposes, the oak tree.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Oh. Someone has just handed me a flashlight. I don't think I should use it. Back to you.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Kim. We've been asked to repeat that. The porch light is on.

clips.title: The Numbers Station Is Owed Geese

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Numbers Station at one hundred and six point six has announced, once again, that it is owed geese.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It has not said by whom. It has not said how many. It has said seven, seven, four, which experts believe is either the amount, the deadline, or simply something it likes to say.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Goose farmers report record demand. Geese themselves report feeling watched.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We reached a debt counselor in the eastern Overlap.

lines.speaker: Debt Counselor
lines.text: My advice is, if you think you might owe the Numbers Station geese, you probably do. Don't send ducks. It knows the difference. It always knows the difference.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Listeners who believe they may owe geese are asked to have them ready, and to keep them calm.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: And now, the markets.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Tuesday futures closed slightly up, on rumors that Tuesday might actually happen this week.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The exchange rate between today and tomorrow is holding steady at one to one, though analysts warn that tomorrow is starting to look expensive.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Gravity rose, then fell. Gravity always does that. We have asked it to stop.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Shares in Grumbel's Ladders climbed. It's what they're for.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: And the central bank of the Overlap has cut interest in everything to zero. The bank says it is not worried. The bank says it is mostly just bored.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That's the markets. Hold on to something.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Residents across all timelines continue to report that the moon is looking at them. Tonight, for the first time, the moon has sent a spokesperson. He joins us by phone.

lines.speaker: Spokesperson for the Moon
lines.text: Thank you, Dale. I'd like to begin by saying that the moon is not looking at you.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Then what is it doing?

lines.speaker: Spokesperson for the Moon
lines.text: The moon is looking near you. There's a difference.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Many listeners say they can feel it.

lines.speaker: Spokesperson for the Moon
lines.text: The moon has a lot of feelings, Dale. Some of them land on people. It isn't personal. It's tidal.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Does the moon have a message for our listeners?

lines.speaker: Spokesperson for the Moon
lines.text: It does. The moon says, sleep well. The moon says, you look nice from up here. The moon says, close your curtains if you'd like, but it will know.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That was a spokesperson for the moon. The moon continues to look near you.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Polls have closed in the Overlap, where voters chose between two candidates who are, by every available measure, the same man.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: He has won. He has also lost. Both of him gave speeches at the same time, from the same podium, and agreed on almost everything.

lines.speaker: The Winner
lines.text: My friends. Tonight, we won.

lines.speaker: The Loser
lines.text: My friends. Tonight, we lost.

lines.speaker: The Winner
lines.text: I want to thank my opponent, who ran a clean and honest campaign.

lines.speaker: The Loser
lines.text: I want to thank my opponent, who has my exact mother.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Turnout was one hundred percent, as both candidates voted for each other. The new term begins on Monday, or, for the losing candidate, doesn't.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The queue at the Bureau of Infinite Queues has today reached the sea. Kim Harrowgate is at the back of it. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm at the very end of the queue, which as of this morning is standing in about four inches of water. The queue began, as far as anyone knows, before chairs.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: With me is a gentleman who has been waiting longer than most. Sir, what are you queueing for?

lines.speaker: Man in the Queue
lines.text: I don't remember. But I'm close. I can feel it.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: How long have you been here?

lines.speaker: Man in the Queue
lines.text: My grandfather held my place, and his mother held his. We take turns sitting down. It's very organized.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: And how's morale?

lines.speaker: Man in the Queue
lines.text: Oh, wonderful. You meet people. My wife was standing in front of me for thirty years before I said hello.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, someone has just handed me a ticket. It says, number nine billion and four.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Hold on to that, Kim. It's a good number.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Science now. Researchers at the Institute for Looking Closely say they have discovered a brand new color, never before seen by any eye in any timeline.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The color is beige.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It is a second beige.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Researchers describe it as slightly warmer than beige, slightly sadder than beige, and impossible to tell apart from beige by anyone who has not trained for eleven years.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It has been named Beige Two. Paint companies are said to be very excited. Nobody else is. Scientists have asked the public to remain calm, which the public says will not be a problem.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: For the four thousandth night in a row, the relay station at the far edge of the dial has broadcast a single question. Is anyone receiving this.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Multiverse Broadcast Authority confirms the station is operated by one man, Teodor, who is in good health, in good spirits, and has a kettle.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Authority reminds listeners that if you happen to hear him between stations, it is polite to say yes.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We tried to reach Relay Four ourselves this evening.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Is anyone receiving this. Hello. This is Relay Four—

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We'll keep trying. Teodor, if you're listening. Yes.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A Tuesday has been found in a drainage ditch outside Precinct Nine of the Damp Dimension. It is mostly intact, with some damage to the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Police believe it is the same Tuesday reported missing last spring, after which most of the eastern Overlap went straight from Monday to Wednesday, and complained about it for months.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The morning is in good condition. The lunch hour is waterlogged. The afternoon appears to have been chewed.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: If this is your Tuesday, please claim it at the Lost and Found desk. Please bring proof of the Monday before it.

clips.title: Vox Pop: The End of the World

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: With the end of the world scheduled, once again, for later this week, we sent Kim Harrowgate out to ask people how they feel about it. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Thanks, Dale. I'm on the high street. Sir, how do you feel about the end of the world?

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.text: Which one?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: The one on Thursday.

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.text: Oh, that one. I'm against it. I've got a dentist appointment on Friday and I'd like to cancel it myself.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Thank you. Ma'am? How do you feel about the end of the world?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Is this the request line?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: No, ma'am, it's the news.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh. Well, while I have you. It goes dum, dum, da dum. And then a man cries.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I don't think I know that one.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Nobody does, dear. That's the problem.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: And you, young man?

lines.speaker: Young Man
lines.text: I think it'll be fine. It always ends on a Thursday, and then on Friday it's still there.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: There you have it, Dale. Cautious optimism, and a song.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: An update on the end of the universe. The universe continues to end at its current rate, which experts describe as leisurely.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Lounge at the End of Time reports that last orders have now been called for the eleven billionth consecutive year. Patrons are said to be unconcerned, and a little sleepy.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Scientists estimate the universe will end completely in roughly a very long time. Asked to be more specific, they said a very, very long time, and then asked if we'd like a drink.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The universe itself was unavailable for comment. It is, however, looking lovely this evening. Warm colors. Very flattering.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Health news. For the first time in recorded history, doctors in four separate realities have agreed on something.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: They will not say what. At a joint press conference, they declined all questions, shook hands for a very long time, and seemed, to observers, enormously relieved.

lines.speaker: A Doctor
lines.text: We just think it's nice. That's all. We'd like to enjoy it for a little while before we say.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: In other health news, a new study confirms that people who drink eight glasses of water a day are mostly water. More on that as it develops.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Earlier this month we reported that a man has been named employee of the month here at Every Possible News for the four hundredth consecutive month, despite not working here. He joins me now in the studio.

lines.speaker: Employee of the Month
lines.text: Thank you, Dale. It's an honor.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: You don't work here.

lines.speaker: Employee of the Month
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Then how do you keep winning?

lines.speaker: Employee of the Month
lines.text: I come in on the first of the month. I stand near the wall by the water cooler. I nod at people. People assume.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That's all?

lines.speaker: Employee of the Month
lines.text: Sometimes I carry a folder.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: What's in the folder?

lines.speaker: Employee of the Month
lines.text: Another, smaller folder, Dale. You never let them see the folder.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: You have a parking space.

lines.speaker: Employee of the Month
lines.text: I don't drive. I just like knowing it's there.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: He will be back on the first.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: In the hill town of Lower Stilt, gravity has been leaking upward since the early hours. Kim Harrowgate is there. Kim, what can you see?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I can see everything. I'm about forty feet up. Most of the town is up here with me. The clock on the clock tower is now a little higher than the clock tower, and the clock tower is being very good about it.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Engineers believe the leak started at a bakery, where someone left the gravity on overnight.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim, are you safe?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, a man floating past has just handed me a brick. I'm holding the brick. I feel wonderful. I feel like a person who is holding a brick.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Don't let go of the brick, Kim.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I won't, Dale. It's all I have.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Residents of Lower Stilt are advised to hold on to something heavy, or someone sensible.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Diplomatic talks between our world and the Mirror World broke down this afternoon, when both delegations reached for the same pen.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Each side accuses the other of copying.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Each side accuses the other of copying.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Observers say the talks had been going well, with both parties agreeing on everything at exactly the same moment, until a junior delegate on the Mirror side was seen, very briefly, scratching his nose with the wrong hand.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Talks resume on Thursday, which in the Mirror World is called Yadsruht, and is considered unlucky.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We have sad news tonight. The word whom has died, peacefully, in its sleep, at the age of nine hundred and twelve.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Whom was a quiet word. It never pushed itself forward. Most people, if we're honest, were never quite sure when to use it, and so, eventually, they didn't.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It is survived by who, which never really understood it, and by a small number of very careful letters to the editor.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Whom will be missed. By whom, we're not sure.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The funeral is on Friday. Please don't bring flowers. Bring a semicolon, if you still have one. It's what whom would have wanted.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Tonight, for the first time, we go live to tomorrow, where Kim Harrowgate has been standing since this morning. Kim, what's it like?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, it's a lot like today. Everyone looks a little more tired. The coffee is the same coffee.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Is there any news?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, you're going to want to sit down for this.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: I am sitting down, Kim.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Then you'll be fine.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim. What is the news?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I can't tell you, Dale. It would spoil it. But wear a coat.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Oh. Somebody's handed me a newspaper. It's tomorrow's. Oh. Oh, that's nice. Back to you, Dale.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We'll find out what's nice tomorrow. At eleven.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: And now, news from around the dial.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: On Deep Space Whalesong, Captain Hum has issued a statement that the whales are fine. Nobody had asked. Captain Hum asks that nobody ask.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: At Snail Jams, traffic on the leaf has been stationary for four days. Shelley Shellbourne describes conditions as brisk.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Moon Dub Sound System reports that a shout out sent last Tuesday has still not come back. Selector Crater says he'll give it another eleven seconds.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: And the Department of Hold Music says your call is important to it. It has asked us to tell you that. We have now told you that.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Property news. Haunted houses are now selling for more than unhaunted ones, as buyers increasingly seek what estate agents are calling, company.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We spoke to a ghost who has lived in the same house since before the street had a name.

lines.speaker: A Ghost
lines.text: We're very quiet. We mostly rearrange the spoons. People find it comforting, knowing somebody's home.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Is there anything you'd like buyers to know?

lines.speaker: A Ghost
lines.text: We don't do the chains anymore. That was a different generation. And please stop painting over the cold spot. We like the cold spot.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Asking prices for a three bedroom with a cold spot now start at four hundred thousand. Spoons included.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Business news. The Grumbel family, makers of fine ladders for eleven generations, today unveiled a ladder with no top.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Company chairman Arnold Grumbel says the new ladder, called the Ambition, has been in testing for three years, and that the test climber is still going, and sends postcards.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: We get a postcard every month. The last one just said, nice view, still going. That's all you want from a ladder, really.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Asked what happens when a customer reaches the top, Mister Grumbel said, there isn't one, and smiled for a while.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders sponsor this program. We have been asked to say, up is a choice.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: In sports. At Coliseum Zero tonight, the final score was a color. Fans of the losing side say it was more of a mood.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Sunball season continues, with the ball, a small and polite sun, said to be in good form and apologizing less.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: And the world hide and seek championship has entered its forty first year, with the defending champion still not found. Officials say they are not worried. Officials say she is very good.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: For full results, ask Chip Thunderbuckle on the Impossible Sports Network. And then ask somebody else.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A man in the eastern Overlap has been fined for returning a library book that has not yet been written.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The library says the book is overdue, in the sense that the author is.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The man, who asked not to be named, says he enjoyed the book, but found the ending rushed, and has left a note in the margin asking the author to take her time.

lines.speaker: A Librarian
lines.text: We don't mind early returns, as such. We mind that he's folded the corner of page two hundred, and she hasn't got there yet. It'll be a shock for her.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The author has been informed, and says she will take it under advisement. Eventually.

clips.title: Weather and Traffic Across All Timelines

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Time now for weather and traffic, across all timelines. Here's Skip Daley. Skip?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Thanks, Dale! Well, it's a beautiful night across most of the timelines. In the northern realities, clear skies and a light breeze. In the southern realities, the sky is looking back at you, so give it a wave!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Out west, expect scattered Tuesdays, mostly in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And a heads up for commuters. There's a ten mile backup on Interstate Zero, where traffic is being held up by a single, very polite deer. Nobody wants to go first!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Skip. What about the weekend?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The weekend has been cancelled, Dale! But the weekday is being extended, so that's nice!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Skip.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Good morning, commuters! Traffic and travel across all timelines, brought to you by Grumbel's Ladders. When the road won't go, go up!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: On Interstate Zero, the polite deer is still there, and it's now been joined by a second, equally polite deer. They've both been saying after you since about four this morning. Expect delays!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The hour between nine and ten is jammed solid, so if you can, skip it entirely and take ten fifteen instead. It's lovely. It's practically empty.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And if you're traveling backward today, please allow extra time. You'll need it. You'll have already needed it!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Weather time! A warm front of nostalgia is moving in from the west tonight, bringing light reminiscing, scattered photo albums, and in some areas, the smell of a house you lived in as a kid.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: That should clear by morning, leaving mild regret, with patches of feeling fine about it, actually.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Further north, a cold snap of common sense. Bundle up! Make good choices!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Overnight lows of around minus one feeling. Highs tomorrow, a pleasant seven or eight out of ten.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Skip. I'll be wearing a coat.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Good call, Dale!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Skip, what's the outlook for the Damp Dimension?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Dale, it's going to rain! That's not a forecast. That's a culture!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Rain has been falling over Precinct Nine for about four thousand years, and our models show it continuing for at least the next four thousand. After that, the models get a bit sad and stop.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Look out for rain coming up from the puddles late tonight. That's normal there. The locals call it giving back.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And my friend Drizzle over at Rainfall FM tells me she's got a new umbrella. Her first one in eleven years. It's yellow!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good for Drizzle.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Allergy sufferers, I'm sorry to say the pollen count is high today. The pollen count is very high. The pollen count has taken the high ground and is refusing to negotiate!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Experts say the pollen isn't hostile. It's just very, very committed to the idea of more flowers.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The ultraviolet index is a four. Ultraviolet is optional this week, so wear it if you like.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Skip, did you say the pollen is negotiating?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: No, Dale. It's refusing to. It's got a list of demands. It's mostly bees.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Your late night tide report! High tide tonight at about eleven. It'll go out at four, and come back at six, with a friend.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Space weather now. The sun is having a big week, folks. Some flares, some moods. Give it space. It'll come around. It always comes around, that's kind of its whole thing!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And on the comet beach, surf's up! Waves of pure time, three to four minutes high. If you wipe out, you'll be fine, you'll just be a little bit earlier.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Skip. Somebody tell the sun we're thinking of it.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Skip, what's the weather doing?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Dale, I honestly don't know. The forecast is fog, so I can't see it.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Is there anything you can tell us?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: I can tell you it's very nice in here! It's soft, it's quiet, and somebody's left a bicycle. I think it's my bicycle. I think I've been in here since Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The fog should lift by morning, at which point I'll be able to tell you what the weather was.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Skip, are you broadcasting from inside the fog?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: I'm broadcasting from the fog, Dale, or the fog is broadcasting from me. Honestly, it's hard to say. Back to you!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Traffic update! The deer on Interstate Zero has finally gone first!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Repeat, the deer has gone first! After nine days of saying after you, it simply looked both ways, nodded to the traffic, and stepped off the road.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Unfortunately, everyone was so moved that nobody has moved. Traffic is now held up by about four thousand people being very proud of a deer.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Skip, is the deer all right?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The deer is great, Dale! It's in a field! It's having the best day of its life!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Evening drive time! Traffic across all timelines is brought to you by Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Westbound lanes on the Overlap Bypass are moving well, and so, unusually, is the road. It's drifted about forty feet to the left, so steer to match!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: There's a slowdown on the bridge to yesterday. Everyone wants to go back. Nobody's allowed. Please turn around safely.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And there's a stalled moment at the junction of Fourth and Forever. Crews are on the scene, trying to get it going again with a gentle cough.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Otherwise, a smooth ride home, folks. Wave at the other versions of you in the next lane!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Skip. The long range forecast.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Sure thing, Dale! Next week, mild. The week after, mild, with some feelings. The month after that, honestly, Dale, a lot can happen.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Next year looks lovely. There's a stretch in the spring where it's warm and nobody's in a hurry. Mark your calendars.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And in about forty years there's a really nice Thursday. I won't tell you why. You'll know it when you're in it.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Skip. I'll look forward to that Thursday.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: This just in. Something has happened. We'll tell you what, as soon as it stops.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Breaking news. Tuesday has arrived early in the eastern Overlap. Please be ready. Please look busy.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We interrupt this program to correct an earlier report. The moon is looking at you. We regret the error.

clips.title: Breaking: Kim Has Been Handed Something

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Breaking news. Kim has been handed something. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: It's a goose, Dale.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Do not give it to the Numbers Station.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: This is the Midnight Edition, on Every Possible News. It is eleven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It is still eleven o'clock. We checked.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A reminder, at this late hour, that the Midnight Edition is not a different programme. It is the same news, read more slowly, in case you were tired the first time.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We find it sinks in better. Some of it sinks in further than we would like.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Several listeners have written to ask why the Midnight Edition begins at eleven. It doesn't. It begins at midnight. It is simply always eleven.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We have asked the clock to explain itself. The clock has asked for privacy at this difficult time.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim. It's nearly midnight. Where are you?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I'm at home, Dale. In my dressing gown. Someone's just handed me a cup of cocoa.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Who?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: My mum, Dale. That one I'm keeping.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good night, Kim. The Midnight Edition continues.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: This is Overnight with Kim. It's three in the morning, I'm standing in it, and somebody has just handed me a lamp.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: On the overnight it's just me and the night desk. The night desk is a desk. It's very supportive. It has held everything I've ever been handed.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Tonight that's a lamp, a small accordion and a sleeping cat. The cat has been very good about the accordion.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: People ask what it's like, reporting at three in the morning. Mostly, Dale's asleep. So when I say back to you, Dale, it goes to a little answering machine.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: In the morning he listens to all of them, with a coffee. Back to you, Dale.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: He'll get that one at seven.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: A man just stopped to ask if I was all right, standing out here in the dark with a microphone. I said I was fine.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: He handed me a scarf. It is the first thing anyone has ever handed me that I actually needed.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Thank you, sir. Back to me.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Good morning, every timeline! I'm Skip Daley, I've been up since four, and the deer is already on the road!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Here's your breakfast checklist, folks! Kettle on? Keys found? Shoes on? Are both of the shoes yours? Check that one. We've had reports!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And if you're having breakfast in more than one timeline, chew in all of them. It's only polite!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Quick one from Interstate Zero. The polite deer is back on the road, and this morning he's brought his mum!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: They're both saying after you. To each other. It's lovely. It's a lot. Leave early!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Skip. It's six in the morning.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Isn't it great, Dale?

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It is always eleven, Skip.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Not for the next three hours, Dale! I asked the clock nicely, and it said I could have the morning!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: I'll be in my office. Where it is eleven.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good evening. This is Every Possible News. Here is the news, from every possible tonight.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: This is Every Possible News. I'm Dale Quarterly, and these are the headlines. Some of them are true here.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The news now. Please remain seated. Please remain calm. Please remain.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good evening. Something has happened in every timeline tonight. Here are some of the somethings.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good morning. It is eleven o'clock. Here is the morning news, which is the evening news, earlier.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: This is Every Possible News. I'm Dale Quarterly. I have been handed some papers. Let's see what they say.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: This is the Midnight Edition. Here is tonight's news.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Slowly.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: And now, the news, brought to you by Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. So, it turns out, is the news.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good evening, or good night, or whatever you've decided it is. Here is the news.

clips.title: The Man Who Lives in His Door

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: In the eastern Overlap, a man has been found living inside his own front door. He says it started as a draught excluder, and things got out of hand.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: He is in good health. He asks that visitors knock gently, as it is also his ceiling.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Science. Researchers have confirmed that time flies when you're having fun, and have measured it. The figure is about eleven percent.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: When you're not having fun, time walks. It stops to look in shop windows. Researchers say there is very little to be done about this.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Reports of a riot in the hill town of Lower Stilt. Kim Harrowgate is there. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm in the town square, where about four hundred people are rioting very quietly. Their signs say, sorry to be a bother.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Someone has just handed me a sign. It says, only if it's not too much trouble.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: What are their demands?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: A second bench, Dale. Near the fountain. For the afternoons.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Kim. We wish them well with the bench.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Property. A house in Precinct Nine has been sold with somebody else's memories still in the attic.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The new owners say they don't mind. Overnight, they attended a wedding they don't remember going to, and say the speeches were lovely.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Overlap Weather Office says it has lost track of Wednesday. It was last seen leaving Tuesday at the usual time.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: If you see Wednesday, please do not approach it. Simply let it pass, as you normally would.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim Harrowgate is at the Overlap Lost Property Office, where something important has been handed in. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, it's me. Someone found me standing outside and handed me in. I've been given a ticket. I'm on a shelf, between an umbrella and a trombone.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Are you all right?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I'm fine, Dale. It's very peaceful. Nobody's handing me anything. I'm the thing.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We'll come and collect you, Kim.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Bring the ticket, Dale.

clips.title: The Night Bus Stops for Tea

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Transport. The night bus that goes through every reality has been delayed, after stopping in one of them for a cup of tea.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Passengers say they understand. Several have stayed for a second cup. One has got married.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The moon has been seen lower than usual this week. Kim Harrowgate is underneath it. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, it's very big from here. It's looking near me. It's looking very near me. It looks tired, Dale.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Has the moon said anything?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: No. But it's handed me a little bit of light. I'm going to keep it in my pocket.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Kim. Do bring it back.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Health. Doctors in four realities, who agreed on something last month for the first time in history, now disagree about what it was.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: They describe the experience as healthy. They describe each other as wrong.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Office of Fair Geese reports that the Numbers Station received four geese this week, all from one woman, who says she doesn't think she owed any, but wanted to be on the safe side.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Numbers Station has thanked her. In numbers.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Traffic is moving on Interstate Zero for the first time in nine days. Kim is at the roadside. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, the cars are going past slowly, and the polite deer is standing on the verge, watching them go. It looks very proud of everyone.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: A driver has just handed me a sandwich out of his window. He said, for the deer. The deer doesn't want it. I'm eating it, Dale.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Kim.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Business. Shares in silence rose sharply this afternoon, after a long period of saying nothing.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Analysts say silence remains undervalued. Silence declined to comment, which analysts describe as very much its strength.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A bench in Founders Park has been dedicated to a man who is still very much alive. He says he is touched, and comes to sit on it every afternoon, to see how it's doing.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The plaque reads, he liked this bench. He says it's accurate.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Tuesday found in a drainage ditch last spring has been claimed. Kim Harrowgate is with its owners. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm with a family in the eastern Overlap who have finally got their Tuesday back. They're having it now. It's a little damp. The afternoon still has bite marks.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: They've handed me a piece of it. It's about twenty past two. It's lovely, Dale.

clips.title: The Sun, as an Exam Subject

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Education. Schools in the Damp Dimension have added a new subject, the sun, which most pupils have never seen.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The first exam was this morning. Most pupils drew a lamp. One drew a very confident orange. He has been given top marks, and a hat.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Local government. A cat in the eastern Overlap has been elected to the parish council, after nobody else stood.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: In his first meeting he knocked the agenda off the table and slept through the budget. Colleagues describe it as the most productive session in years.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: In Lower Stilt, a man has spent the week climbing a Grumbel's Ambition, the ladder with no top. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, he's shouted down that there isn't a top, which we knew. But he says there's a very nice landing about halfway up, with a chair. He's having a sit down.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: He's lowered a basket. Someone has put a sandwich in it. Up is a choice, he says. So is staying where you are.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Astronomy. A new star has been reported, low in the sky over the eastern Overlap.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: On closer inspection it is a porch light. Astronomers say they have decided to count it anyway.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The arts. The Mirror World's national gallery has opened an exhibition of paintings of our world. Critics there describe our world as charming, but backwards.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Critics here have described the exhibition as charming, but backwards. Both sides are delighted.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Nobody's Bakery, which sells bread that nobody made, has been found to have somebody in it. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm in the bakery with a woman in an apron, covered in flour. She says she's been doing it every night for thirty years.

lines.speaker: Maureen, a Baker
lines.text: I don't mind the name. I'd just like someone to say thank you, now and then.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: She's handed me a loaf. It's warm, and it sings when you squeeze it. Thank you, Maureen.

clips.title: A Man Who Likes It at Lost and Found

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The Overlap Lost and Found desk reports a record week. Nine hundred umbrellas, four hundred gloves, and a man who says he isn't lost, he just likes it there.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: He has been given a chair and a ticket. Staff say he's no trouble, and very good at finding things.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That's the news. More at eleven. It is always eleven.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That's the news, from every possible tonight. Some of it may even be yours.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That is the news. Hold on to something. Or someone sensible.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That's all from the newsroom. Please return to whatever you were doing. It's still there.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Nothing else has happened. If anything does, we'll let you know. Probably at eleven.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That was the Midnight Edition. Go to bed. The news will keep. It always has.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Every Possible News. Up is a choice. So is the news. Thank you for choosing it.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That's the morning news. Have some breakfast. And somebody tell the sun we're thinking of it.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Weather and traffic now, across all timelines. Skip?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Thanks, Dale!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: It's weather time, folks, in every timeline at once! Let's see what's falling!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Skip Daley with your weather and travel, brought to you by Grumbel's Ladders! When the road won't go, go up!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Good morning, commuters! Here's what's happening out there, and in there, and over there!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Your late night weather, folks! Grab a blanket! And maybe a second, smaller blanket!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Out west, scattered Tuesdays, heavier in the afternoon. If you get caught in one, just keep going! You'll come out into Wednesday eventually!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: On Interstate Zero, the polite deer is back on the road, and nobody wants to go first. Expect delays of about one deer!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: A warm front of nostalgia is drifting in from the east, bringing scattered photo albums and the smell of a school hall. It'll clear by morning. But you'll ring your mum, so that's nice!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Fog in the low-lying timelines tonight! If you can't see your hand in front of your face, don't worry. It's still there! It's probably holding something!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: In the Damp Dimension, rain! I'll say that again for the folks at the back. Rain! Four thousand years and counting! Drizzle says hi!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Over on the comet beach, waves of pure time, three to four minutes high, with a strong undertow toward last week. Swim between the flags, folks!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The moon is looking near you tonight. So if you feel watched, that's just the moon! Give it a wave! It loves that!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: There's a stalled moment at the junction of Fourth and Forever. Crews are on the scene. Please be patient! It's a lovely moment, and nobody's in any hurry to leave it!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The long range forecast! Next week, mild. The week after, mild, with feelings. After that, folks, honestly, a lot can happen. That's what's so great about weeks!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Space weather! The sun has had a big week. Some flares. Some moods. Give it room, folks. It'll come round. That's literally its whole job!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The pollen count is high, and the pollen count knows it. Sneeze responsibly, folks! Into your elbow! Bless you! Bless all of you!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: That's your weather! Back to you, Dale!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Skip.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Stay dry, stay warm, and if you're traveling backward, leave early! You'll already have left!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: That's weather and traffic, folks! Drive safe, and wave at the other versions of you!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Skip. I'll take an umbrella.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Take two, Dale!

clips.title: Teodor Is Heard, Part One: The Receiver

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Night four thousand and one at Relay Four, and tonight, at last, an explanation.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Engineers at the Multiverse Broadcast Authority have examined the signal from the relay at the far edge of the dial. Teodor's transmitter is in perfect working order. It is his receiver that is broken.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It failed in a storm, eleven years ago. Since then, Teodor has been able to ask, but not to hear. Every yes said to him in eleven years has gone nowhere.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim Harrowgate is at the Authority. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm with an engineer who has listened to Relay Four every night for a decade.

lines.speaker: Broadcast Engineer
lines.text: The signal's beautiful. You can hear his kettle. He puts it on every time he asks, in case somebody comes round.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Can his receiver be fixed?

lines.speaker: Broadcast Engineer
lines.text: Not from here. Somebody would have to get a yes through the hard way. Louder, or closer, or stranger.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, someone's just handed me a piece of paper. It just says, yes. People have been leaving them on the doorstep here for years. There are thousands.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We'll keep trying, then. Teodor, if you're listening, and you are. Yes.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Is anyone receiving this. This is Relay Four. The kettle's on.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We know, Teodor. We know.

clips.title: Bev Gets Her Song, Part Two: Lift Number Two

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A woman who has spent eleven years looking for a song has asked us for help. Her name is Bev. She heard it once, in a lift. Kim Harrowgate is in the lift. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm in lift number two at the Grand Overlap Hotel, which has been out of order for eleven years. Someone has just handed me the out of order sign. With me is the manager.

lines.speaker: Hotel Manager
lines.text: It was a lovely lift. It had carpet. It had a little seat. It had the music.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Where did the music come from?

lines.speaker: Hotel Manager
lines.text: Down the line from Relay Four, like every lift in the Overlap. Requests, birthdays, a little flute in the afternoons. Then one spring night the line went quiet, and every lift went silent at once.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Eleven years ago?

lines.speaker: Hotel Manager
lines.text: Eleven years ago.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim, is Bev there?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: I'm here, love. In the corner. This is the one. Between floors four and five. Three hours we were stuck in here, me and my Stan.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Bev, did you know the music came from Relay Four?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Relay Four? Isn't that the man who keeps asking if anyone can hear him?

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It is. Teodor, if you're listening, a lady would like a word. Back to you, Kim.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I'm handing this sign back, Dale. Out of order. Hopefully not for much longer.

clips.title: Greg Comes Home, Part Ten: The Long Bridge

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A shadow has been sighted on the long bridge into the eastern Overlap, heading east at about four in the afternoon. Kim Harrowgate is on the bridge. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm halfway across, and so is he. At this time of day he's about forty feet long, so he's technically on both banks at once.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Is it Greg?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: It's Greg. He's let me walk beside him, as long as I don't stand in his light. Greg, why so slowly?

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I want to get there at noon. He stands in the sun at noon. So there's room.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Greg, it's four o'clock. That's twenty hours.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I was behind him for forty one years. I can wait twenty hours in front.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, the sun's going down. He's getting thinner. I can barely see him.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I can't walk in the dark. Nobody tells you that, about being a shadow.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Somebody has just handed me a flashlight. Dale, the last time I was handed a flashlight near Greg, I didn't use it.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Use it, Kim.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: He's back. He's very long. He's pointing straight down the road into the eastern Overlap.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Could you walk with me? Just to the end of the bridge?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm going to walk a shadow home.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Take as long as you need, Kim. The porch light is on. And for the next mile or so, so is Kim.

clips.title: Teodor Is Heard, Part Twelve: Relay Seven

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We interrupt this bulletin, which had not yet started. We go live to Relay Four.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: This is Relay Four. Relay Seven, the relay ship Nightjar, I'm told you're out there. I'm told there's somebody on the night shift.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: There's a light on my board that hasn't been on for eleven years. It's on now.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: If that's you, I'm going to open the line all the way. People have been saying it for eleven years. Let's hear them.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I can hear you, love.

lines.speaker: Selector Crater
lines.text: Moon hears you, Teodor.

lines.speaker: Numbers Station
lines.text: Four. Four. Four.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales say yes. The whales are fine.

lines.speaker: Mara, Dimension Hop
lines.text: We said it four seconds ago, Teodor. Keep up.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: I could always hear you. Go to sleep.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello? Is this the request line?

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Yes. Yes it is. Hold on, Bev.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: I heard all of that. Every one of you.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: I had a speech, the first year. I've forgotten it. So, just this. Thank you. The kettle's on. It has always been on. Come round.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Teodor. From all of us at Every Possible News. Yes.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: I heard that, Dale.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: I heard that.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Good evening. This is Every Possible News, in costume. I have come as a man who is not frightened. It's a very good costume.

clips.title: A Night in the Most Haunted House

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Halloween. Kim Harrowgate is spending the night in the most haunted house in the eastern Overlap. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, it's two in the morning, and nothing has happened. A ghost has just handed me a cup of tea and asked if I'm warm enough. She's put the heating on.

lines.speaker: A Ghost
lines.text: We don't do the chains any more. That was a different generation.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Are you frightened, Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Only of how nice it is, Dale. I may not leave.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The Halloween forecast! A big full moon, light fog, and scattered howling, mostly from people stepping on plugs in the dark!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And if a bedsheet comes down your street and says boo, say boo back, folks. It's only polite!

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Breaking news. A moon is missing. Every possible timeline agrees that one moon has gone, and no two timelines agree on which.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim Harrowgate is standing where it used to be. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, it's very dark here. Somebody's just handed me a torch.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: We are receiving reports that everywhere, at once, smells faintly of toast.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: The source has not been identified. Officials ask that you check your own toaster, and then, gently, everyone else's. More at eleven.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A song is stuck in the head of every listener in every timeline. Nobody knows how it ends.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: I've got it, Dale! Ba, ba ba, ba... and then...

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: That is where it stops for everyone, Skip. More at eleven.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: There has been a knock at the newsroom door. Three knocks. We have checked. There is nobody there.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Stations across the dial report the same. The door has been asked to comment. It has declined.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: For a few seconds, the sky was a colour our science desk cannot name. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, it was like... I haven't got it. Somebody's just handed me a paint chart. It's none of these.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A pigeon has walked into the newsroom. Sources say the same pigeon is in every studio on the dial.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: It has nodded at me twice, as if we went to school together. We did not. More at eleven.

clips.title: Review: The Quiet Corner with Greg

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Arts. Early on Sunday morning, the Lounge at the End of Time broadcast the first Quiet Corner with Greg, a shadow. Our critic listened at full volume, with the windows shut.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Her review reads, in full: bold, spare, I think he said hello. Four stars.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Telephone engineers report that a switchboard last staffed in nineteen forty six has begun lighting up again. Callers say they reached it by accident, while turning a radio dial.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim Harrowgate is with one of them. Kim?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Dale, I'm with a woman who got through. She'd been listening to an agony aunt, then to us, then to that new traffic report, out past the edge of the dial. All in about a minute.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: And a voice said, number, please. She's handed me the receiver, Dale. It's still warm.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Thank you, Kim. We have tried this ourselves. We got the traffic. More at eleven.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Navigation. The Multiverse Broadcast Authority reports that several relay ships are drifting from their usual courses. Officials describe the drift as within tolerance. Asked whose tolerance, officials said, ours.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: As the ships drift, listeners report new stations coming in above one hundred and eight. So far: disco, a courtroom, and traffic for a wormhole.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Space weather! The relay ships are drifting a little tonight, so if you hear new stations out past one hundred and eight, that's not interference, folks. That's neighbours! Give them a wave!

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: That was Overnight with Kim. I'm stepping off the seam.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: The lamp is going home. So am I, Dale. Not yet.

clips.title: The Seam Between Tuesday And Wednesday

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: The news, from the place where the night is stitched. It's just gone three. I'm on the corner where Tuesday and Wednesday share a pavement, and the streetlights can't agree which night it is.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: A bus from Thursday stopped on the Wednesday side, and nobody got off, because nobody was sure which day the fare belonged to. The driver handed me the timetable. It has two Thursdays, and no Friday.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: He said Friday called in sick. I believe him. Friday has looked tired all year.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: If your street has a seam in it, step over, not on. I'm standing on this one so you don't have to. It's very quiet. The quiet is the story. Back to me, until five.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: On the overnight desk there's the lamp, the scarf, and a minute somebody handed me at the seam. The minute is warm. I've put it in my pocket.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Don't tell Dale. He has strong views about loose minutes. He thinks they should be filed under eleven.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I'll give it back at dawn, if dawn is still where we left it. Here's the night, continuing.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Overnight with Kim. You're on the night desk.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Kim. It is three in the morning. I was asleep. The answering machine has you standing in a seam. Seams are carpentry. This is a newsroom.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: It's both, Dale. The pavement is Tuesday on my left and Wednesday on my right. I'm on the line. Somebody handed me the line. It's a bit of string, and a timetable.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Put the string down. Come back to the building. It is always eleven in the building. It is never a seam. I am saying this from the hallway, in my dressing gown, and I am not pleased.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: You're on the phone, Dale. The phone is also a seam. It joins your hallway to my corner. Go back to sleep. I'll file it when you wake.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: I will wake at eleven.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: You always do. Goodnight, Dale.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: He'll get that one with his coffee. The seam is still here. So am I.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: A woman just walked out of Wednesday, bought a paper from Tuesday, and went back the way she came. The paper was tomorrow's. She seemed used to it.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: She handed me the crossword. Half the clues are from a day we haven't had. I'll do the ones I can.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: If you're awake on the wrong side of a night, you're in the right place. Stay with me until the streetlights pick a side.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: That's the morning, every timeline! Eat something, even if your world has packed a bag.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: I'm Skip Daley. I'll be here tomorrow, if tomorrow is still on.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Good morning to the timeline where the moon resigned! Lovely send-off! They gave it a cake! The cake is still in orbit, and it is smiling! Bring a fork if you're visiting!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Good morning to the timeline where the sea stood up and left! Beautiful weather for a walk, if you don't mind the gap! The gap has put out deckchairs!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And good morning to the timeline where Tuesday never arrived! You get a long Monday, folks, and Monday has packed sandwiches! Eat them! Monday worked very hard!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: The polite deer got out, by the way. He evacuated politely. He held the door for the flood. The flood said thank you. That's your breakfast bulletin. Isn't it great?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Quick checklist for anyone whose sky is doing something new! Coat on? Shoes on? Are the shoes from this timeline? We've had mix-ups, and the other shoes walk by themselves!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: If your world ended overnight, you still get breakfast. That's the rule. I wrote it on the board. The board is slightly on fire. The rule held.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: More mornings, after these messages, and after the deer lets the traffic through. He's being very generous. Leave early!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Good morning, you're on the breakfast line! It's a beautiful day in at least one timeline!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: Skip. It is six in the morning. You are describing the end of several worlds as if they were a picnic. I am in the hallway. I was promised eleven.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: It is a picnic, Dale! They brought sandwiches! The sandwiches survived! The world is the one that left, and it left a note, and the note says have a lovely day!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: A note from an apocalypse is not a weather report. Come back to the desk. Use your indoor voice. Several indoors have just ceased to exist.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: That's why I'm chipper, Dale! If I do it quietly, people think it's worse than it is! The cake is smiling! The deer held the door! Somebody has to say well done!

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: I am going back to bed. When I wake, it will be eleven, and none of this will have been cheerful.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Sleep well, Dale! I'll save you a sandwich from the timeline with the long Monday!

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: He loves it really. You can hear it in the dressing gown. Right! Who else has ended, and would like a shout-out?

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: And in our own timeline, wonderful news. The sun turned up. I am personally taking that as a compliment. It did not have to. Several suns, elsewhere, have taken the morning off.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Traffic on Interstate Zero is the polite deer, his mum, and a small queue of people applauding a hole in the sky. The hole is bowing. Let them have their moment, then go around.

lines.speaker: Skip Daley
lines.text: Kim is still out from the overnight. She has handed the night desk a warm minute and a crossword from Friday. Friday is feeling better. That's the news, and it is, I think you'll agree, gorgeous.
